lastCompletedStory.title: Wire the container lane onto a named counted waiver in the in-container harness

openQuestions: CAM-432 (still out of scope, untouched by this story) needs to delete the now-provably-dead `test.skipIf(!xAvailable)(...)` gates once each binary is confirmed a true hard dependency everywhere in CI.

scripts/cam/plan-verdict-report.json (US-002 plan review) flagged that the PRD's own container-lane definition ('.devcontainer AND the ci-container job') is broader than what US-006 actually wires (only scripts/test-in-container.ts's docker exec invocation); .devcontainer/devcontainer.json's containerEnv still declares no CAM_TEST_WAIVERS, so any bun test/check:all run driven directly inside the devcontainer (not through this harness) still hits the unwaived preflight and fails -- this is unchanged by US-006 and was explicitly out of this story's acceptance criteria (AC1 names only scripts/test-in-container.ts's docker exec call as the injection site). Flagging for reviewer-judgment: either file a follow-up to add the waiver to devcontainer.json's containerEnv, or accept that in-container non-harness runs are intentionally red (container-mode workers running their own quality gates go through a different path per patterns.md:1004, so this does not affect CAM-152/185 container-mode workers, only an ad-hoc interactive `bun test` run inside a bare devcontainer shell).
nextStoryContext: US-006 finalizes CAM-424's container lane (the last piece of this PRD). scripts/test-in-container.ts now exports buildContainerTestExecArgv(containerName) -- a pure builder returning ['exec', '-e', 'CAM_TEST_WAIVERS=tmux,pgrep,uuidgen', containerName, 'bun', 'test'], mirroring the existing build*ExecArgv convention in container-firewall.ts/container-auth.ts/container-config.ts -- consumed by makeDefaultExecFn's real spawnSync call. `ps` is deliberately absent from CONTAINER_WAIVED_DEPS: it's already 'legitimate-environmental' in test/helpers/test-deps.ts, so depPreflight skips it without ever consulting a waiver. runInContainerTests gained a new injectable readExpectations seam (defaults to a real read of test/helpers/lane-expectations.json rooted at cwd) and now returns { summary, skipCheck, exitCode }: skipCheck is checkSkipCount(summary.skip, expectations.lanes.container.expectedSkips, 'container') (reused verbatim from US-005's scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts, not re-derived), and exitCode is 1 when EITHER fail>0 OR skipCheck.ok is false. The stale top-of-file comment ('A run with only skips (fail count 0) exits 0.') and the equivalent policy line in runInContainerTests's own docstring were both rewritten to describe the new dual condition (AC3's 'both sites'). Proven live on real Docker (cam-worker container already running, repo bind-mounted at /workspace, so no rebuild was needed to see uncommitted changes): waived run `bun scripts/test-in-container.ts` = 5680 pass / 0 fail / 40 skip, exit 0 ('container lane: 40 skip (matches recorded expectation)'); unwaived run `docker exec cam-worker sh -lc 'cd /workspace && bun test'` = 5677 pass / 3 fail / 40 skip, REAL_EXIT=1, the 3 fails being exactly US-002's tmux/pgrep/uuidgen preflight tests (5680 = 5677 + 3, confirming the waiver is the only variable that flips them). test/helpers/lane-expectations.json's container block is now FINAL (no longer provisional): expectedSkips 40, passFloor 5680, measuredVia records both real runs. Host lane's passFloor was also bumped 5716->5720 (this story's own 4 new tests: 1 skip-mismatch exit-code case + 3 buildContainerTestExecArgv cases) -- expectedSkips stayed 0, still enforced by US-005's check:skip-ratchet gate (verified green: 'host lane: 0 skip (matches recorded expectation)'). Full check:all spine green (16 gates incl. skip-ratchet). scripts/file-size-budget.json raised scripts/test-in-container.ts 223->293 and test/test-in-container.test.ts 366->439 (gate-measured actuals), dated US-006/CAM-424 note prepended to _ref. This appears to be the final story of the CAM-424 PRD (all US-001 through US-006 as originally scoped); the open question above about devcontainer.json's containerEnv is the only loose end flagged for reviewer-judgment, not a new story requirement invented here.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed -e/--env on `docker exec` is scoped to the exec'd process only ('only valid for the process started by that docker exec command, and aren't available to other processes running inside the container'), never the container's persistent env. Matches the implementation's use of -e for a per-invocation, per-run waiver declaration rather than baking it into devcontainer.json's containerEnv.
